title: Dependencies
concept: Dependencies declare external crates your project requires
why: Modern software is built on shared libraries. Rather than rewriting an HTTP client or JSON parser for every project, you declare dependencies and the package manager fetches them. This leverages community work, reduces duplication, and keeps your project focused on its unique logic.
theory: Dependencies are declared in `package.xi` under the `dependencies:` section. Each entry maps a crate name to a version constraint (semver). XIOM resolves the full dependency graph: it fetches each crate, resolves its transitive dependencies, detects version conflicts, and produces a lockfile (`xiom.lock`) with exact pinned versions. Dependencies can also be git-based (`git: "https://..."`) or path-based (`path: "../sibling"`) for local development.
code_template:
package my_app
  version: "0.1.0"
  target: binary

dependencies:
  xiom_json: "^0.4"
  xiom_net: "^1.0"

# Run: xiom pkg install
# Then: use xiom_json in your code
solution:
package api_client
  version: "0.1.0"
  target: binary

dependencies:
  xiom_net: "^1.2"
  xiom_json: "^0.5"
  xiom_cli:
    git: "https://github.com/axiom/cli"
    tag: "v2.1.0"
  local_utils:
    path: "../shared/utils"
tips: Run `xiom pkg outdated` to see which deps have newer versions
Use path dependencies during development of multiple crates
Commit `xiom.lock` for binaries, omit for libraries
common_mistakes: Adding a dependency to `package.xi` but forgetting to run `xiom pkg install`
Using `*` as version — never do this in published crates
